title: Gianduiotto
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Turin's iconic hazelnut chocolates, their distinctive upside-down boat shape formed by hand or mold while the ganache is still pliable, made from a smooth blend of chocolate and finely ground toasted hazelnuts.
longDesc: Gianduiotto was born in 19th-century Turin, reportedly created to stretch scarce cacao supplies by blending in the region's abundant hazelnuts, a happy substitution that became the foundation for what is now one of Italy's most beloved chocolate traditions, including the spread it later inspired.
ingredients: 150 g (1 cup) hazelnuts, toasted and skins removed
steps: Grind the toasted hazelnuts in a food processor until they form a smooth, oily paste, scraping down as needed.
Melt the milk chocolate gently over a double boiler.
Combine the melted chocolate with the hazelnut paste, powdered sugar, and softened butter, mixing until smooth and glossy.
Pour the mixture onto a sheet of parchment paper and spread to an even thickness of about 1cm.
Chill in the refrigerator until firm enough to hold a shape but still pliable, about 1-2 hours.
Cut into small triangular or rectangular pieces and shape each by hand into the traditional upside-down boat form, or press into a gianduiotto mold.
Chill again until fully set before serving.
chefTips: Grinding the hazelnuts thoroughly into a smooth paste, rather than leaving them coarse, is essential for the classic silky gianduiotto texture.
Work with the mixture while it is still slightly pliable but firm enough to hold a shape - too cold and it will crack rather than shape neatly.
A gianduiotto-shaped mold gives the most authentic look, though hand-shaping works well too.
commonMistakes: Under-grinding the hazelnuts, leaving a gritty rather than silky-smooth texture.
Letting the mixture get too cold before shaping, causing it to crack rather than form neatly.
Using dark chocolate instead of milk chocolate, which changes the traditional flavor balance.
storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool place for up to 2 weeks.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Hazelnuts provide healthy fats and vitamin E, best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: Gianduiotto originated in 19th-century Turin and remains one of Piedmont's most cherished chocolate traditions, later inspiring the famous hazelnut-chocolate spread that shares its name.
